# Task 1: **Design and Configure the AWS Networking Infrastructure**

This section details the successful deployment of the foundational AWS networking

architecture required for the application. A **custom Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)** was

configured with a well-planned CIDR block to securely host the infrastructure. To ensure

high availability and fault tolerance, **6 subnets were provisioned and distributed evenly across 2 Availability Zones**. This architectural setup includes **2 Public Subnets** for the Web Tier, **2 Private Subnets** for the Application Tier, and **2 Private Subnets** for the

Database Tier—with each subnet sized to support at least 256 IP addresses.

For external connectivity, an **Internet Gateway (IGW)** was created and attached to the VPC to route public traffic.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Secure outbound internet access for the private tiers was established by deploying a **NAT Gateway (associated with an allocated Elastic IP)** within one of the Public Subnets.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Finally, traffic routing was effectively segregated by creating **three distinct**

**Route Tables (Public, Private Application, and Private Database).** These tables were

accurately mapped to their respective subnets with the necessary routes configured for both internal communication and internet access.

&nbsp;

The screenshots verifying the successful creation, configuration, and association of

all the above resources are provided below.

# Task 2: **Deploy the Web Tier (Presentation Layer)**

This section details the successful deployment and configuration of the application's Web Tier. To establish the presentation layer, **Amazon EC2 instances were provisioned** and launched **within the previously created Public Subnets**. Dedicated Security Groups were configured and attached to these instances to securely regulate inbound traffic. Following the infrastructure provisioning, secure connections were established to the instances to install the Nginx web server. **The provided HTML application files were then modified with some extra refinement by me and successfully copied and deployed to the server directories.** Finally, the deployment was validated by confirming that the web application is fully accessible and rendering correctly via the public internet.

The screenshots verifying the EC2 instance creation, Security Group configurations, Nginx installation, and the live accessible web page are provided below.

![][image6]![][image7]![][image8]

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

# Task 3: **Deploy the Application Tier (Backend API)**&nbsp;

This section outlines the deployment and configuration of the backend Application Tier. To host the backend logic, **Amazon EC2 instances were provisioned securely within the Private Application Subnet**. Secure remote access to these private instances was established **via a Bastion Host**. The runtime environment was configured by installing Python 3, Flask, and all required package dependencies as specified in the project repository. The primary application code (app.py) was then deployed to the instances. **Notably, the Python application was enhanced by implementing a custom GET API endpoint designed specifically to fetch feedback data.** Finally, the Flask application was **successfully initialized on port 5000,** and its operational status and internal connectivity were **verified**.

The screenshots verifying the private EC2 instance creation, secure connection setup, dependency installation, and the running Flask application (including the GET API response) are provided below.

![][image9]![][image10]

&nbsp;

# Task 4: **Deploy and Configure the Database Tier**

This section details the provisioning and configuration of the secure data persistence layer. A managed **Amazon RDS MySQL instance was created and strategically deployed within the isolated Private Database Subnets to ensure maximum security**. Database credentials and access parameters were configured according to the project requirements. Following the infrastructure setup, **a secure connection to the database was established directly from the Application Tier (EC2 terminal)**. The provided SQL commands were then executed via the terminal to initialize the database schema and structure. Finally, seamless end-to-end backend communication was validated by **successfully verifying the connection between the Python Flask application and the MySQL database.**

The screenshots verifying the Amazon RDS instance creation, database subnet deployment, and successful Flask-to-Database connectivity are provided below.

![][image11]

![][image12]![][image13]![][image14]

# Task 5:  **Implement Network and Instance Security**

This section outlines the implementation of robust network and instance-level security across the architecture. **Dedicated Security Groups were created and configured with strict inbound and outbound rules to enforce the principle of least privilege**. Custom security configurations were applied independently across all architectural layers, specifically for the Load Balancer, Web Tier, Application Tier, and Database Tier. To ensure secure internal communication and protect the infrastructure against unauthorized access, **network traffic was tightly restricted, ensuring that only the strictly required ports are permitted** to communicate between the respective tiers.

The screenshots verifying the precise inbound and outbound rule configurations for all the respective Security Groups are provided below.

# Task 6:  **Configure the Internet-Facing Application Load Balancer**

This section covers the setup of an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to efficiently distribute incoming public traffic. **A Target Group was created** , and the frontend Web EC2 instances were successfully registered to it. The ALB was securely attached to the Public Subnets, and the application's accessibility was validated by successfully **reaching the frontend application via HTTP using the ALB's default DNS name**

# Task 7: **Configure Internal Application Load Balancer**

This section describes the deployment of an Internal Application Load Balancer (ALB) to securely manage and route traffic between the frontend and backend layers. An **internal ALB was provisioned along with a dedicated Target Group configured with appropriate health checks.** **The backend Flask EC2 instances (Application Tier) were successfully registered to this Target Group.** Finally, seamless and secure internal **communication was validated to ensure that the Web Tier can successfully route requests to the Application Tier.**&nbsp;

# Task 8: **Configure Nginx Reverse Proxy for API Routing**

This section covers the configuration of the Nginx web server to act as a reverse proxy. **The default Nginx configuration was replaced with the custom nginx.conf** provided in the project repository. **This configuration was updated to securely route all backend API requests from the frontend Web Tier directly to the Internal Application Load Balancer.** The Nginx service was subsequently restarted, and successful end-to-end communication between the frontend and backend tiers was verified.

# Task 9 & 10: **Integration and Validation**

This section focuses on the **final integration between the backend Application Tier and the Database Tier.** The **Flask application's configuration was updated** with the accurate Amazon RDS connection details. Following this update, **the successful connection between the application and the database was verified.** T**o validate the complete end-to-end data flow, sample feedback was submitted through the frontend web application,** and it was confirmed that the submitted data was successfully processed and stored within the database.&nbsp;
